summary: The missions, work, runtimes and attention lists now follow this node's own writes within about one fold, as the agents roster has since its local-commit wake. A claim this node commits cuts each refresher's pause to its floor, 100 ms or twice as long as the last fold took, whichever is longer. Before, these lists folded on a fixed one-second pace, so a write waited up to a second plus a fold to appear. That is most of the remaining 'publish missions' latency in projection-fresh. One shared scanner per daemon reads each commit once for all five refreshers, agents included, off the writer. Commits that hold only replicated claims keep the one-second pace. Pausing twice the fold after a local claim keeps a cheap fold to about a third of a core, even under a stream of local writes.

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay change.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes or migrations.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule, registry or coordinated member upgrade change.

compatibility.detail: Readers, the published lists and their cuts are unchanged; only how soon a refresh follows a local commit changes. The agents roster now pauses twice its last fold after a local claim, instead of once.

downtime.detail: Takes effect on the next daemon start.

manual.detail: To see it, read the 'publish missions', 'publish work', 'publish runtimes' and 'publish attention' paths of /v1/client/request-latency after the roll. Their p99 should drop toward one fold. The per-refresher cpu labels (published_list.missions, published_list.work, runtimes/refresh, publication.attention, published_list.agents) should stay near their earlier levels.

recovery.detail: Rolling back restores the fixed one-second pace for the four lists, and the agents roster's own look.
